testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When backing your vehicle into an alley, what should you do first?

options.text: Drive directly into the alley parking space.
Turn your vehicle right to face the alley directly.
Drive past the alley and stop at a right angle to it.
Drive past the alley and stop parallel to it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive past the alley and stop parallel to it.
questions.explanation: To back into an alley, first drive past it and stop parallel to the outer edge. Then back your vehicle straight into the alley parking space.

questions.question: What should you do in a large truck to avoid slowing down traffic?

options.text: Change gears while driving uphill.
Pass other vehicles while driving uphill.
Stay in the right lane as much as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the right lane as much as possible.
questions.explanation: If your heavy truck cannot keep up with traffic speed, stay in the right lane.

questions.question: What is a tank endorsement?

options.text: Required only for transporting gases.
Required only for transporting liquids.
Required for transporting both liquids and gases.
Optional when transporting hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required for transporting both liquids and gases.
questions.explanation: You need a tank endorsement to drive a tank vehicle that carries liquids or gases.

questions.question: What should you do if you're unsure how to handle a vehicle fire?

options.text: Use water.
Stay inside the vehicle.
Wait for firefighters to arrive.
Keep the engine running.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for firefighters to arrive.
questions.explanation: If you don't know how to safely put out a fire, wait for firefighters. This is especially important with hazardous materials fires.

questions.question: Why do some air brake systems use alcohol?

options.text: To prevent ice from forming in the air brake valves.
To make the compressor work better.
To lubricate parts of the braking system.
To prevent rust on the air brake valves.

questions.correctAnswerText: To prevent ice from forming in the air brake valves.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have an alcohol evaporator that adds alcohol to the system. This prevents ice from forming in the brake valves.

questions.question: Why is texting while driving dangerous?

options.text: It causes both mental and physical distraction.
A message may upset the driver.
Texts may be more interesting than driving.
It is slower than making a phone call.

questions.correctAnswerText: It causes both mental and physical distraction.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is dangerous because it distracts you mentally and physically.

questions.question: When should you use your turn signal?

options.text: Signal before you turn.
Turn off the signal before you turn.
Signal only if vehicles are ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal before you turn.
questions.explanation: Always signal well before turning. This tells other drivers your plans so they won't try to pass you. Without a signal, other drivers may think you are just slowing down or stopping.

questions.question: If the low air pressure warning light comes on while driving, what happens?

options.text: Your brakes will work only if there is enough air left in the tanks.
You can brake 14 times before the air runs out.
You can continue driving normally and check the brakes later.
You can continue driving with your emergency flashers on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your brakes will work only if there is enough air left in the tanks.
questions.explanation: When the low air pressure light comes on, stop and park your vehicle safely as soon as possible. Your brakes will only work as long as air remains in the tanks.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, which of these is NOT acceptable for air and electrical lines?

options.text: Air hoses are making a hissing noise.
Air hoses and electrical lines are not cut.
Air lines are not pinched.
Air lines are not dragging against tractor parts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air hoses are making a hissing noise.
questions.explanation: During inspection, listen for leaks in air hoses. Air hoses and electrical lines must not be cut, frayed, spliced, or worn. They must not be tangled, pinched, or dragging against tractor parts.

questions.question: What should you do when backing with a trailer?

options.text: Do not back in a straight line.
Wait until you are far off course before correcting.
Pull forward to reposition the vehicle as needed.
Avoid using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward to reposition the vehicle as needed.
questions.explanation: When backing with a trailer, pull forward to reposition your vehicle whenever needed.

questions.question: What skills test might you be asked to perform during a basic vehicle control test?

options.text: Swerve to avoid a hazard.
Parallel park.
Drive straight into a parking space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parallel park.
questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test includes many parking and backing maneuvers. These include straight line backing, offset back/right parking, offset back/left parking, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: What does it mean if the safety relief valve in the air brake system releases air?

options.text: The compressor needs more air.
The air pressure is too high.
The brakes are working correctly.

questions.correctAnswerText: The air pressure is too high.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air from the tanks when pressure gets too high. If the valve releases air, something is wrong with the system. A mechanic should check it.

questions.question: What should you do before driving down a steep hill?

options.text: Shift into a higher gear.
Take your vehicle out of gear.
Shift into a lower gear.
Use only the brakes to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift into a lower gear.
questions.explanation: On steep hills, use the engine's braking power as your main way to control speed. Slow down and shift to a lower gear before going down the hill. Using only brakes can cause them to overheat and stop working well.

questions.question: At 55 mph on dry pavement, how many feet does brake lag add to your stopping distance?

options.text: 32 feet
45 feet
20 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 32 feet
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance has four parts: perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet to the total stopping distance.

questions.question: When should you not use the parking brake?

options.text: When the brakes are very hot.
When the brakes are very cold.
When there is snow on the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the brakes are very hot.
questions.explanation: After coming down a steep hill, your brakes will be hot. Do not use the parking brake until the brakes cool down. Using it while hot can damage the brakes.

questions.question: What is the purpose of air tank drains?

options.text: Allow rain water to enter air tanks.
Remove water and oil from air tanks.
Should never be opened.
Must stay open while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and oil from air tanks.
questions.explanation: Air tanks have drains that remove water and compressor oil from the system. If water and oil build up, they can damage the air brake system.

questions.question: What is true about a distracted driver?

options.text: Usually follows the rules of the road.
Usually notices hazards more slowly.
Is a good person to follow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually notices hazards more slowly.
questions.explanation: Distracted drivers see hazards on the road more slowly than focused drivers. Sometimes they do not see hazards at all.

questions.question: Is a low air pressure warning signal required on vehicles with air brakes?

options.text: No, it is not required.
Yes, it is required.
It is optional.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is required.
questions.explanation: All vehicles with air brakes must have a low air pressure warning signal. If the signal goes off while driving, stop the vehicle and have the system checked by a mechanic.

questions.question: How do you test the low pressure warning signal?

options.text: Engage and disable the parking brake.
Press and release the brake pedal quickly many times.
Open the rear shut-off valves.
Uncouple and recouple all glad hands.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and release the brake pedal quickly many times.
questions.explanation: To test the warning signal, first let the system charge. Then press and release the brake pedal quickly many times. This removes air from the system. The warning signal should come on when pressure drops to a dangerous level.

questions.question: What is an advantage of using an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS)?

options.text: Makes stopping distance shorter.
Speeds up brake response time.
Provides less control.
Provides more control.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provides more control.
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) stops wheels from locking up during hard braking. This gives you better control of the vehicle. However, it may not shorten stopping distance.

questions.question: When doing pre-trip inspections, what should you do?

options.text: Do the inspection the same way every time.
Check different items each time.
Check items in a different order each time.
Skip some items each time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do the inspection the same way every time.
questions.explanation: Do your pre-trip inspection the same way every time. This helps you remember to check everything important.

questions.question: After driving over a bridge during the driving test, the examiner may ask you to recall what?

options.text: The posted weight limit.
The color of a sign you passed.
How many traffic lanes were on the bridge.
If there was a crosswalk on the bridge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The posted weight limit.
questions.explanation: The examiner may ask you to remember the weight limit posted on the bridge.

questions.question: On an uphill grade, gravity will:

options.text: Speed your vehicle up.
Slow your vehicle down.
Not affect your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow your vehicle down.
questions.explanation: Gravity slows your vehicle down when going uphill. You may need to shift to a lower gear to climb a steep hill.

questions.question: Which surface is the most slippery?

options.text: Dry ice
Wet ice
Wet pavement

questions.correctAnswerText: Wet ice
questions.explanation: Wet ice forms when it gets slightly warmer and melts a little. Wet ice is much more slippery than dry ice.

questions.question: A convex mirror is sometimes called a ____ mirror.

options.text: Bug-eye
Square
Helper

questions.correctAnswerText: Bug-eye
questions.explanation: Large vehicles often have curved convex mirrors called "bug-eye" mirrors. These show a wider view than flat mirrors. However, they make objects look smaller and farther away than they really are.

questions.question: A sign your brakes need repair is when:

options.text: The brake pads are not covered in grease.
The brake pads are not covered in oil.
The brake pads are worn thin.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brake pads are worn thin.
questions.explanation: Check your brakes for cracked drums, shoes or pads with oil or grease on them, and worn or broken shoes.

questions.question: To get a hazardous materials endorsement, what must you do?

options.text: Give your fingerprints and pass a background check.
Provide your last five years of work history.
List all countries you visited in the last 10 years.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give your fingerprints and pass a background check.
questions.explanation: You must submit your fingerprints and pass a background check to get a hazardous materials endorsement.

questions.question: When parked on the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Rely on your taillights to warn other drivers.
Not worry about other drivers.
Turn on your four-way emergency flashers to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way emergency flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: Turn on your four-way emergency flashers when stopped on the side of the road, especially when it is dark or foggy. Place warning devices within 10 minutes.

questions.question: What shows how much air pressure is in your vehicle's air tanks?

options.text: The supply pressure gauge
The ABS malfunction lamp
The tractor protection valve

questions.correctAnswerText: The supply pressure gauge
questions.explanation: Vehicles with air brakes have a supply pressure gauge. This gauge shows the driver how much air pressure is in the air tanks.

questions.question: A driver who stops at a green light could be:

options.text: An impaired driver.
A color-blind driver.
A driver who does not know the rules.

questions.correctAnswerText: An impaired driver.
questions.explanation: Watch other drivers for signs of impairment. Drivers who have been drinking, are tired, are using drugs, or are sick can be dangerous. One sign of impairment is stopping at green lights.

questions.question: What does rough acceleration do?

options.text: It is recommended.
It can damage the engine and transmission.
It is required on slippery roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can damage the engine and transmission.
questions.explanation: Always speed up slowly and smoothly. Rough acceleration can damage your vehicle's engine and transmission.

questions.question: When driving downhill, your vehicle will:

options.text: Slow down.
Travel at the same speed as on flat road.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up.
questions.explanation: Gravity makes your vehicle go faster when driving downhill. Slow down before you reach a downhill section.

questions.question: When driving a truck that requires a CDL, you must:

options.text: Never wear a seat belt.
Wear a seat belt only if you are carrying more than 500 pounds of cargo.
Always wear a seat belt.
Wear a seat belt only if you are driving a tank truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always wear a seat belt.
questions.explanation: You must wear a seat belt at all times when operating a commercial truck. This is required by law.

questions.question: A commercial motor vehicle must have:

options.text: A fire extinguisher only if carrying hazardous materials.
A fire extinguisher only if driving through remote areas.
No fire extinguisher.
A fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment.

questions.correctAnswerText: A fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment.
questions.explanation: All commercial motor vehicles must have proper emergency equipment. This includes a fire extinguisher, reflective triangles or flares, and spare fuses.

questions.question: Bridges usually:

options.text: Do not freeze.
Have heaters to prevent freezing.
Freeze before other road surfaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Freeze before other road surfaces.
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before regular road surfaces. Be extra careful on bridges when temperatures are near freezing.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing during the driving test, you should:

options.text: Pass a slow vehicle on the tracks.
Get out of the vehicle to check for a train.
Not change gears while on the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not change gears while on the tracks.
questions.explanation: During the driving test, do not stop, change gears, pass other vehicles, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on railroad tracks.

questions.question: A thin layer of ice on the road surface is called:

options.text: White ice.
Black ice.
Blue ice.

questions.correctAnswerText: Black ice.
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice on the road. The road shows through it, making it look wet. Be careful when temperatures are below freezing and the road looks wet.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a tire problem to check for?

options.text: Using radial and bias-ply tires together
Recapped tires on the front of a school bus
Tread separation
All tires are made by the same company

questions.correctAnswerText: All tires are made by the same company
questions.explanation: Check tires for low or high pressure, excessive wear, cuts, tread separation, mismatched sizes, radial and bias-ply tires used together, damaged valve stems, and recapped or retreaded tires on school bus front wheels. It does not matter if all tires are made by the same company.

questions.question: Which of the following is poor lane usage during the driving test?

options.text: Not driving over curbs or sidewalks
Stopping behind crosswalks
Driving in the left lane when multiple lanes are available
Finishing a right turn in the right lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving in the left lane when multiple lanes are available
questions.explanation: During the driving test, stay in the right lane on roads with multiple lanes. Do not cross curbs, sidewalks, or lane markings. Stop behind stop lines and crosswalks. Complete turns in the correct lane.

questions.question: Which of the following means brakes need repair?

options.text: Brake pads are not covered in grease.
Brake pads are not covered in oil.
Brake shoes are worn too thin.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake shoes are worn too thin.
questions.explanation: Check brakes for cracked drums, shoes or pads covered in oil or grease, and shoes that are missing, broken, or worn too thin. Worn thin brake shoes mean the brakes need repair.

questions.question: What is the maximum safe play on a 20-inch steering wheel?

options.text: One-quarter of an inch.
Two inches.
10 inches.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two inches.
questions.explanation: A steering wheel with more than 10 degrees of play may be defective. On a 20-inch wheel, 10 degrees equals about two inches of movement at the rim.

questions.question: How much water must be on the road for hydroplaning to happen?

options.text: Usually several inches
A good amount, such as a large puddle
A small amount

questions.correctAnswerText: A small amount
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs when tires lose grip and slide on a layer of water. Only a small amount of water on the road is needed for this to happen.

questions.question: Water and compressor oil in an air brake system should be:

options.text: Kept in the system for proper brake function.
Added if the amount is low.
Removed regularly.
Not a concern.

questions.correctAnswerText: Removed regularly.
questions.explanation: Compressed air in air brake systems contains water and oil. These can damage the brakes if they build up. Open the air tank drain manually each day to remove this buildup.

questions.question: When entering traffic, does a large vehicle need more or less space than a car?

options.text: Less space than a car.
About the same space as a car.
More space than a car.

questions.correctAnswerText: More space than a car.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles need more space to enter or cross traffic than smaller vehicles. They are larger and need a longer distance to accelerate.

questions.question: At speeds under 40 mph, maintain at least ____ of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle's length.

options.text: One second
Two seconds
Three seconds

questions.correctAnswerText: One second
questions.explanation: At speeds under 40 mph, allow a minimum of one second of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle's length. At faster speeds, add at least one more second.

questions.question: How do states verify that a CDL or CLP driver has only one license?

options.text: By calling surrounding states.
By using a computerized system that connects all states.
By asking the driver.
By looking through the driver's wallet.

questions.correctAnswerText: By using a computerized system that connects all states.
questions.explanation: All U.S. states share CDL and CLP license information in a computerized database. When you apply for a license, the state checks this database to make sure you don't already have one in another state.

questions.question: When driving on surfaces with poor traction, why should you accelerate slowly?

options.text: Because it is always good practice to accelerate slowly.
To avoid losing control of the vehicle.
So you don't go faster than the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: To avoid losing control of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: On surfaces with poor traction, such as rain or snow, accelerate slowly to maintain control of your vehicle.

questions.question: What is a header board used for?

options.text: To help the driver see behind them.
To protect the driver from moving cargo.
To provide extra storage space.
To prevent the driver from leaving the tractor.

questions.correctAnswerText: To protect the driver from moving cargo.
questions.explanation: Header boards, also called "headache racks," protect drivers from cargo that moves during a crash or emergency stop.

questions.question: Where must the malfunction lamp be located on a dolly with ABS?

options.text: On the rear
On the left side
On the front
On the top

questions.correctAnswerText: On the left side
questions.explanation: A dolly with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) must have a yellow malfunction lamp on its left side.

questions.question: What happens if an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) malfunctions?

options.text: The driver will not know.
A yellow lamp will light up on the instrument panel.
The brakes will lock up.
The brakes will not work.

questions.correctAnswerText: A yellow lamp will light up on the instrument panel.
questions.explanation: A yellow malfunction lamp on the instrument panel will turn on to alert you if the ABS is not working properly.
